recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. If the ResourceList ambiguity reappears, investigate the current Kindling/publisher generator and generated artifact pipeline; no FHIR core source edit is needed for FHIR-14210 now.
issue_request: FHIR-14210 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core STU3 issue, auto-approved after pointing to a community forum report about invalid generated JSON Schema. The linked report said a contained Practitioner matched multiple ResourceList oneOf branches because abstract/permissive Resource and DomainResource schemas were included, and suggested removing DomainResource, Parameters, and Resource from ResourceList.
initial_application: No commit explicitly mentions FHIR-14210. Jira records Grahame Grieve's 2018-08-16 comment that the issue had already been done. The relevant implicit application is the January 2018 JSON Schema generator repair trail, especially commits 4757010487355c7ad9910dc788395f5a1d37d167 and 05bfe5879059bdbd9f7dee5594f67ec819c8c85e, which changed the old generator to constrain resourceType, set additionalProperties false, filter ResourceList to concrete resources, and update schema publication wiring.
additional_context: The old Java SchemaGenerator was removed from this core checkout in 2021 when the build switched to the Gradle Kindling dependency. Current build-scoped downloads and validation pages still link the generated fhir.schema.json.zip. A current build.fhir.org schema check found no Resource or DomainResource refs or definitions in ResourceList, one concrete Parameters branch, and resourceType consts for Practitioner and Parameters. The later same-change-family FHIR-17696 issue is already audited on the combined branch as no-change.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current FHIR core source correctly exposes the generated JSON Schema artifact, and the current generated artifact no longer exhibits the ResourceList ambiguity reported by FHIR-14210; generated schema behavior now belongs in the Kindling/publisher pipeline rather than a checked-in core schema file.
